title: METEOR v8.0: evidence-weighted reaction selection reconciles enzyme prediction with growth feasibility
description:
Code and deposited results for the PSB 2027 submission METEOR: Evidence-weighted reaction selection reconciles enzyme prediction with growth feasibility.

METEOR takes a per-protein EC confidence matrix, aggregates it into reaction-level evidence, and selects a biomass-feasible reaction set from the ModelSEED universal database with a mixed-integer linear program, then maps the result back onto the protein score matrix through a ranking-preserving update. The cost grades each reaction by the confidence behind it rather than charging every reaction the same: a uniform penalty prunes by count and discards genuine isozymes along with the noise, whereas grading by confidence removes the weak tail and keeps the redundancy the evidence supports.

This is not weighted gap-filling. There is no thresholded draft and no gap-filling stage; every reaction in the universal database competes on the same evidence-derived cost and the whole set is chosen in one optimisation.

The deposit carries the per-genome records behind every reported number, including the 108 MILP solutions the main-text tables are computed from, and three aggregation scripts that regenerate the published figures from the deposit alone.
